subject: Issue with running inla in Linux

messages.author: 18dec7dfc20b2ae1
messages.subject: Issue with running inla in Linux
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to run rinla on the cluster. I've downloaded INLA package successfully and used the inla.binary.install() for a Linux alternative. But when I tested a simple code,

library(INLA)
y= rnorm(10)
df= data.frame(Y=y)
mod= inla(Y~1,family="gaussian", data =df)

 I received an error message saying,
 *** inla.core.safe:  inla.program has crashed: rerun to get better initial values. try=2/2
/home/ywang34/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.2/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/inla.mkl: /home/ywang34/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.2/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/first/libstdc++.so.6: version `GLIBCXX_3.4.30' not found (required by /cm/shared/spack/opt/spack/linux-ubuntu20.04-x86_64/gcc-12.1.0/icu4c-67.1-ol3mpxfu6gaa22lxnsoukci7yv6gpgb6/lib/libicuuc.so.67).

I contacted the IT of my university and was told that "glibc is a core system library, and wholesale upgrading all compute nodes to an experimental version risks breaking the entire cluster.  At that point, the only real solutions are to find an alternative or modify the binary not to require that glibc version"

I am wondering if there is a workaround to resolve this issue.

Yanzhao

messages.author: 18dec7dfc20b2ae1
messages.subject: Re: Issue with running inla in Linux
parts: The issue is resolved with the testing version. Case closed, thanks.
